root_cause.text: In `f2fs_do_zero_range()`, the extent cache update functions are called unconditionally even when the zero range operation zeroed zero bytes (i.e., `index == start`), causing a zero-length extent to be inserted into the extent cache, which triggers a BUG_ON assertion in `__update_extent_tree_range()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a guard `if (index > start)` around the calls to `f2fs_update_read_extent_cache_range()` and `f2fs_update_age_extent_cache_range()` to prevent updating with a zero-length extent. The CVE description states "In error path of f2fs_zero_range(), it may add a zero-sized extent into extent cache," and the crash backtrace shows `kernel BUG at fs/f2fs/extent_cache.c:678` due to "extent len is zero".

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard to only update extent cache ranges when the zero range length is positive.
intent_record.what: Wrapped calls to f2fs_update_read_extent_cache_range and f2fs_update_age_extent_cache_range in a conditional check if (index > start).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the extent cache update functions are now only called when the zero range operation actually produces a non-zero length (index > start), preventing unnecessary or potentially invalid updates for zero-length ranges.

grouping_result.intent: Add a guard to only update extent cache ranges when the zero range length is positive.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes directly address the root cause by adding a guard to prevent updating the extent cache when the zero range length is zero, thus avoiding the insertion of a zero-length extent that triggers the BUG_ON.

candidates.rationale: This unconditional call to update the read extent cache can insert a zero-length extent when index equals start, triggering BUG_ON in __update_extent_tree_range().
This unconditional call to update the age extent cache can insert a zero-length extent when index equals start, contributing to the BUG_ON assertion failure.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call to update the read extent cache is performed unconditionally even when the zero range length is zero (index == start). Inserting a zero-length extent triggers BUG_ON in __update_extent_tree_range().

This call to update the age extent cache is performed unconditionally even when the zero range length is zero (index == start). This also contributes to the insertion of a zero-length extent and the subsequent assertion failure.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function f2fs_do_zero_range unconditionally calls f2fs_update_extent_cache_range(dn, start, 0, index - start) after the loop, even when no blocks were zeroed (e.g., when start == end). This can result in a zero-length extent (len=0), which triggers a BUG_ON in __update_extent_tree_range(). The caller f2fs_zero_range may invoke f2fs_do_zero_range with end equal to start, e.g., when end_offset - dn.ofs_in_node is 0, causing the loop to not execute and index to remain equal to start. The code does not check if index > start before updating the extent cache, so it introduces the vulnerability.
